question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-8) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({5}^{t})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 2 \\ {5}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡5\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & ={t}^{2}\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 2 \\ {5}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡5\end{bmatrix}+2t\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2t-8 \\ {5}^{t}\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 2{t}^{2} \\ {5}^{t}{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡5\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 4{t}^{2}-16t \\ {5}^{t}\cdot 2t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 6{t}^{2}-16t \\ {5}^{t}{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡5+{5}^{t}\cdot 2t\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ {sec}^{2}⁡t \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ 1\end{bmatrix}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ {sec}^{2}⁡t \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}{sin}^{2}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}{cos}^{2}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}{sin}^{2}⁡t-{cos}^{2}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t-\operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t-\operatorname{sec}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

By the scalar function multiple rule, we have
 

$$
(u(t)g(t))^{′}=u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t).
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${g}^{′}(t).$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,2t,\,1⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{t}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & =u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t) \\  & =2\sqrt{t}⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,2t,\,1⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}⟨\sqrt{t},\,{t}^{2},\,t⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4t\sqrt{t},\,2\sqrt{t}⟩+⟨1,\,t\sqrt{t},\,\sqrt{t}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,5t\sqrt{t},\,3\sqrt{t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

(u(t)f(t))^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2t \\ 3{t}^{2}\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)=\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\begin{bmatrix}t \\ {t}^{2} \\ {t}^{3}\end{bmatrix}+\operatorname{ln}⁡t\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2t \\ 3{t}^{2}\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ t \\ {t}^{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ 2t\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ 3{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ t+2t\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ {t}^{2}+3{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

(u(t)f(t))^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t).

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ {e}^{t}\end{bmatrix} \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\begin{bmatrix}2\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ {e}^{t}\end{bmatrix}+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\begin{bmatrix}2\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ {e}^{t}\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ {cos}^{2}⁡t \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ -{sin}^{2}⁡t \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ {cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ {e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
